source_name: OpenStreetMap via Nominatim

source_name: HMEL - Pipeline

source_name: HPCL - Our Refineries

notes: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited is a Government of India public sector undertaking under MoPNG, so its published description of its own refineries is treated at official_india level, the same treatment given to IndianOil (SRC028) and BPCL (SRC031). source_name: Mumbai Port Authority - Citizen's Charter (April 2025 revision)
notes: Corroborating source only, quoted inside NL017: 'There is a Marine Oil Terminal with 5 berths for handling Petroleum Oil Lubricants (POL) at Jawahar Dweep, an island off Mumbai Port. notes: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited is a Government of India public sector undertaking, a subsidiary of IndianOil, so its published description of its own assets is treated at official_india level. source_name: Bharat Oman Refineries Limited - Pre-Feasibility Report for expansion of crude oil storage at Vadinar (MoEFCC environmentclearance.nic.in)
data_type: crude oil terminal, SPM position and pipeline length
notes: BORL's own filing on the Government of India environmental clearance portal. Used to enrich PL005 only; it creates NO edge. It gives the BORL CALM buoy position (Lat. 22o 33' 44'' N, Long. 69o 45' 38'' E, about 7 km offshore from the Vadinar coast) and states a 943 km pipeline to Bina, against the 935 km in BPCL's commissioning announcement (SRC031). Both lengths are preserved and neither was averaged. It also shows that BORL operates exactly one SPM, which is why the Gujarat Maritime Board register entry 'BORL - SPM Sikka Crude oil' (SRC010) and this filing describe one facility under two locality labels. report_date 2013-12-06 is taken from the document's own PDF creation metadata because the cover carries only 'November 2013'. Raw copy archived at data/raw/borl/.

source_name: Reliance Industries Limited - Half-Yearly EC Compliance Report Jamnagar (Apr-Sep 2024)
data_type: refinery EC proposal identity and marine/crude-terminal compliance conditions
notes: Reliance Industries Limited's own compiled half-yearly compliance filing to MoEFCC, hosted on RIL's own website, covering multiple Jamnagar EC proposals (the original refinery under proposal nos. J-11011/25/94-IA-II and J-11011/25/93-IA-II; the 2005 combined-complex expansion to 59.7 MMTPA; the Petroleum and Petrochemical Complex SEZ; and the SEZ refinery's 35.2-to-41 MMTPA expansion) in one PDF. Reliance is a private company, but this is a statutory compliance report to the Government of India's Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, so it is registered at official_india level, the same treatment as SRC032/SRC038/SRC039 for other companies' MoEFCC filings. Source establishing NL022 (PORT016 -> R022): the SPM/SBM, submarine and on-shore pipeline, and Crude Oil Terminal conditions under headings 'A. SPM and Sub-Sea Pipeline' / 'B. CRUDE OIL TERMINAL (COT)' are recorded only against the original ('18 MMTPA'/'RPL...18 to 27 MMTPA') refinery proposal sections; the filing's own dedicated SEZ-refinery proposal (J-11011/149/2007-IA-II (I)) carries no such headed marine/crude condition of its own. CORRECTION (Phase 3 step 2, 2026-08-23): Phase 3 step 1's note above did not examine Condition 12 (Marine/Coastal) under this same filing's THIRD proposal, J.11011/232/2005-IA-II (I) ('Environmental clearance for expansion and modernization of petrochemical refinery complex', 59.7 MMTPA combined, filed from the Reliance Jamnagar SEZ village of Meghpar/Padana), which names 'Crude and product SPMs' among marine facilities augmented 'in consultation with the National Institute of Oceanography', reported as complied. This condition is now also the source for NL023 (PORT016 -> R023) - see network_links.csv for the full evidence and caveats. Raw copy archived at data/raw/ril/ril_jmd_ec_compliance_2024-12.pdf and its pdftotext -layout extraction at data/raw/ril/ril_jmd_ec_compliance_2024-12.txt (the file could not be parsed by the standard web-fetch text extractor).

source_name: Reliance Jamnagar Infrastructure Limited - Consolidated EIA for Petroleum and Petrochemicals Complex at Jamnagar (submitted to MoEF)
data_type: SEZ/JERP refinery project description and shared infrastructure statements
notes: Consolidated EIA document (with clarifications and additional information provided to MoEF, New Delhi, October 2009), sponsor Reliance Jamnagar Infrastructure Limited - an Indian environmental-clearance filing archived on a UK government publishing host, registered at official_india level because its content and origin are the Indian regulatory filing, not the hosting site. Used ONLY as background for the R023 (RPL (SEZ), Jamnagar) finding recorded in docs/network_connectivity_report.md and docs/data_sources.md; it creates NO network_links.csv edge. Its Section 3.11 ('JERP Refinery') states 'The petroleum products from the crude refinery, LOBS will be accommodated in the existing Refinery and the Marine Tank Farm area', and Section 2.7.1 states seawater for the SEZ is sourced 'as in the case of the existing refinery' through 'the existing seawater intake provided at the marine terminal area' - both describing the JERP/SEZ refinery using the pre-existing refinery's Marine Tank Farm and marine terminal rather than a separate one, but neither sentence names a crude-specific SPM/pipeline path for the SEZ refinery, which is why the finding is recorded as PARTIALLY RESOLVED and not converted into an edge. Raw copy archived as text at data/raw/ril/eia_jamnagar_sez_2009-10.txt (pdftotext -layout of the retrieved PDF).
